title: When the First Parents of Our Race
description: When the First Parents of Our Race in Tonic Solfa to ST. AGNES, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book II, composed on divine subjects, hymn 78, headed “Redemption by Christ”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST. AGNES; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: When the first par-ents of our race Re-bell'd and lost their God, And the in-fec-tion of their sin Had taint-ed all our blood;

lines: When the first parents of our race
And the infection of their sin
Aside the Prince of glory threw
And wrapt his Godhead in a veil
His living power, and dying love
And rais'd the ruins of our race
To thee, dear Lord, our flesh and soul
Bless'd Jesus, take us for thy own,
Thine honour shall for ever be
For ever shall our thankful tongue

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST. AGNES by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
